source.title: Hide & Seek: Transformer Symmetries Obscure Sharpness & Riemannian Geometry Finds It
source.citation: Marvin F. da Silva et al., 2025
source.authors: Marvin F. da Silva; Felix Dangel; Sageev Oore

record.tranche_reason: Extends sharpness–generalization-gap correlation measurements to diagonal networks, ImageNet vision transformers, and BERT models using symmetry-corrected geodesic sharpness.
record.gate_note: Rows record reported Kendall rank correlations. The paper also discusses prior studies and reports ablations and relaxation-parameter results; those do not provide separate main-claim outcomes beyond the correlations recorded here.
record.test_reason: The study directly measures sharpness–generalization-gap correlations and finds reversed or absent relationships in several settings. These results qualify extensions of V7 beyond its original convolutional setting; they do not directly contradict the original CIFAR-10/SVHN result.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that symmetry-aware geodesic sharpness strengthens or recovers within-task correlations, but their signs vary: negative on diagonal regression and ImageNet, positive on MNLI. This variability limits predictive and optimization use; stronger absolute correlation does not establish that flatter models consistently generalize better.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares adaptive sharpness with a geodesic sharpness measure that corrects for parameter symmetries; it uses first-order geodesic approximations in the transformer experiments and includes curvature corrections. It is an extension of the sharpness–generalization measurement question, not the same convolutional-family setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The correlation sign varies by setting: negative for diagonal networks and ImageNet, positive for MNLI. Metric choice changes the reported correlation magnitude modestly. The paper reports that ablation effects depend on metric, and varying the relaxation parameter does not significantly affect results.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), 2025
record.problems: The transformer evidence is correlational and based on aggregate model sets; no error bars, confidence intervals, or p-values are reported. The authors state that correlation sign varies by setting, limiting predictive utility. Diagonal-network experiments use synthetic sparse regression data.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy with the same architecture and training recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.

The original convolutional-family setting on CIFAR-10/SVHN without augmentation; ranking against norm- and margin-based measures; perturbation tolerance defined by training-error increases. Transformer training losses are not established as similarly low. The study instead uses loss-increase sharpness at fixed perturbation radii.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

missing.what: MNLI ablations show dependence on the sharpness definition: removing the corrected norm gives τ = −0.15 for the inverse metric and 0.01 for the mixed metric; removing second-order corrections gives 0.22 and 0.24, versus full-method values 0.28 and 0.38. These qualify the positive MNLI results and are not recorded in rows.

record.verdict_notes: All reported main-row numbers match the supplied text. V7 links concern extensions of its sharpness–gap relationship to new settings and alternative measures, not replications of its original convolutional experiment. The geodesic results are eligible evidence because they measure relationships with actual generalization gaps, rather than only reporting a method-performance score.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not tested.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.

The study tests diagonal networks, fine-tuned ImageNet vision transformers, and fine-tuned BERT models, rather than one convolutional family on CIFAR-10 and SVHN without augmentation. It measures geodesic sharpness and adaptive sharpness, not the full set of norm- and margin-based measures in the version.
No memorized-example removal or retraining experiment.

relation.reason: The study directly measures sharpness–generalization correlations across trained networks.

tranche.reason: The measured reversals and absent correlation qualify transfer of the sharpness–gap relationship, while the alternative geometry recovers positive correlation on MNLI.

source_check.notes: The recipe incorrectly describes first-order geodesic approximations: Eq. 4 and Algorithm 1 retain quadratic corrections. The authors' sign-dependent conclusion is accurate; Appendix G supplies methodological ablation controls.

statements.correction: MNLI BERT: inv-metric τ=0.28; mix-metric τ=0.38. Appendix G: separate ablations removing the corrected norm and second-order weight corrections. Appendix H.2: relaxation-parameter sensitivity analysis.
statements.problem: The BERT correlations are correct, but the assertion that the study reports no controls overlooks its methodological ablations.

statements.correction: ImageNet CLIP ViT-B/32: adaptive τ=-0.41; inv-geodesic τ=-0.71; mix-geodesic τ=-0.70. MNLI BERT: adaptive τ=0.06, interpreted as no correlation. Transformer extensions; limits_scope for V7.
statements.problem: The findings are accurate; the challenges classification exceeds V7's stated convolutional scope. These transformer results limit transfer of its directional relationship.

statements.correction: 50 diagonal networks; d=200; training loss 10^-5; 90%-sparse ground-truth vector. Adaptive τ=-0.68; inv-geodesic τ=-0.83; mix-geodesic τ=-0.86. Reversed direction in this extension; limits_scope for V7.
statements.problem: The findings and extension caveat are accurate; the challenges classification should distinguish failure of transfer from contradiction within V7's stated convolutional scope.
